## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (75%)** · Unreliable input · Defer to expert
The reliability flag is set, InSitu is in the 90% set, and MUSK disagrees.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 75%, InSitu 25% | Invasive leads, not decisive |
| Conformal set | InSitu, Invasive (90%) | Two classes unseparated |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.77 / 100th percentile | Flagged; atypical image |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Different top class |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 Invasive [F5] | Mostly supportive |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 3, 4, 10) · ↑ invasive · Above typical; largest concept-model term [F2] · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Scarce here; tubules usually argue against invasive [F3] · Weak
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 2, 3, 5) · ↑ invasive · Scored high; spot check only 3/20 · Unreliable
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (regions 4, 8) · context · Above typical; descriptive only · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Faithful. Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60).
- **Concepts**: Not shown faithful; effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007 includes 0). This case leans on necrosis (Unreliable).

## Could be wrong if
- The degraded, atypical image skews probabilities; the reliability score ranks errors only modestly (AUROC 0.69).
- This is in situ disease: InSitu holds 25%, and MUSK picks a different top class.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 3, 4, 10**: confirm tumor cells infiltrating stroma versus duct-confined disease.
2. **Region 2**: highest-contribution region; check for duct-confined atypia.
3. **Region 7**: look for benign glands or normal lobules.
